US stocks fall as AI doubts ignite tech selloff
articles.description: US stocks tumbled on Thursday and the Nasdaq posted its steepest daily drop since early June as a batch of high-profile earnings reports ignited fresh fears about the AI spending race. The S&P 500 ended deep in negative territory. But the tech-laden Nasdaq, dragged down by microchips, suffered a steeper loss, falling 2.6 percent in the wake of a spate of high-profile AI-related earnings results. The blue-chip Dow eked out a nominal gain minutes before the closing bell. Meta Platforms' results beat analyst expectations, but its stock slid 7 percent as the Facebook parent posted its first cash outflow in more than a decade due to its AI-related expenditures and announced plans to issue non-voting shares in a two-for-one split to raise capital to spend on the nascent technology. Tesla shares fell 3.1 percent even though the electric car maker unexpectedly posted positive free cash flow in the quarter and cut its 2026 capital spending plans. The Philadelphia SE Semiconductor Index, which has driven much of the current bull market's gains, plunged 6.7 percent, its biggest daily percentage drop since June 23. "It's a wonderful day on Wall Street," said Paul Nolte, senior wealth adviser & market strategist at Murphy & Sylvest in Elmhurst, Illinois. "The only part of the market that is really suffering here is technology, which has been the golden child of the markets up until about June." "Investors are starting to realise that there are some holes in the AI story," Nolte added. "And that's having an impact on the indices because they're so heavily weighted toward technology." On the geopolitical stage, Iran-backed Houthis launched new strikes against Saudi targets, sending crude prices to a five-month high. Investors worried that ongoing Middle East strife could keep inflation hot and force the US Federal Reserve to keep raising interest rates. Data from the US Labour Department showed initial claims for unemployment benefits kept drifting along near multi-decade lows. Signs of labour market stability will allow the Fed to focus on fighting inflation. Financial markets are currently pricing in the probability that the central bank will raise its policy rate by another 25 basis points before year-end. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 11 points, or 0.02 percent, to 52,867, the S&P 500 lost 93 points, or 1.2 percent, to 7,663 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 694 points, or 2.6 percent, to 26,008. Third-quarter earnings season is well underway, with 111 of the companies in the S&P 500 having reported. Of those, 83 percent have beaten analyst expectations, according to the most recent LSEG data. Procter & Gamble warned that rising cost pressures would take an increasing bite out of profit, but beat analyst estimates, sending the stock 5.6 percent higher and supporting consumer staples. Blackstone advanced 8.4 percent, after the company said widening credit spreads on AI-related debt could present an opportunity to lock in higher returns. Lockheed Martin climbed 7 percent after the aerospace/defence firm raised its annual sales and profit forecast. Spotify rose 11.1 percent after the Swedish music streaming firm forecast fourth-quarter profit above Wall Street estimates, betting on its AI-powered features to drive user growth. Chipmakers Intel, AMD, Sandisk and Marvell all tumbled more than 8 percent amid the broader semiconductor selloff. (Reuters) Edited by Cecil Wong

The proposed language would combine transaction intents, proof-carrying data and Groth16 proofs. Its purpose is to help applications execute user requests while efficiently verifying that specified conditions have been met. For Cardano bulls, the work creates a new developer narrative around advanced applications and verifiable on-chain actions. A move to $2 would still require substantial new demand, but the target returns ADA to a major psychological level watched across the market. BNB Bulls Build a $1,500 Price Case BNB recently traded near $732, making a move to $1,500 slightly more than a doubling from current levels. The bullish case is tied to the token’s utility across trading, transaction fees and the wider BNB Chain ecosystem, alongside its deflationary burn structure. Cardano and BNB offer established network opportunities, but both already command multibillion-dollar valuations. Remittix offers a different setup: a launch-stage PayFi ecosystem approaching its hard cap with active payment testing, existing product usage and a defined November catalyst. For buyers comparing a $1 ADA forecast and $1,500 BNB prediction with new crypto opportunities, RTX combines a $0.28 entry with an announced $0.46 minimum exchange launch price. The final $3 million represents the remaining presale window before market debut. About Remittix Remittix is developing a connected PayFi ecosystem for crypto-to-bank and bank-to-crypto transactions. articles.title: ECB preview: MUFG sees October hold, two hikes ahead. See EUR/USD year end at 1.12
articles.description: The French-German 10-year spread is the key gauge: MUFG’s scenarios put it at about 170 basis points in its base case and above 200 in a crisis, levels last associated with the euro zone debt crisis. EUR/USD has been tracking the two-year swap spread between the euro and the dollar closely, so any further scaling back of ECB hike expectations is likely to weigh on the currency, while a firm December signal would offer some support. In bonds, heavy redemptions from the ECB’s portfolio in coming months put the pace of quantitative tightening in focus. Any hint of a slowdown could ease pressure on French debt. Energy remains a swing factor: MUFG’s forecasts assume supply risks fade, so persistently high oil and gas prices tied to the Middle East conflict would challenge both its rate path and its call for a gradual euro recovery. --- Earlier: ECB’s Panetta says rising yields a drag on growth, not a crisis, ahead of rate meeting BoE preview: MUFG expects November rate hike as energy shock pushes UK inflation above 4% MUFG expects the ECB to hold next week as higher bond yields and French fiscal stress tighten conditions for it, but still sees two more hikes, with France the biggest risk to the euro. Summary: MUFG says the bond sell-off and French fiscal risks have removed the case for an October ECB rate hike, as officials highlight the drag from tighter financial conditions. It still expects a 25 basis point hike in December and another in the first quarter of 2027, taking the policy rate to 3.00%, then a cut back to 2.75% by the third quarter of 2027. Resilient activity and higher gas prices since September justify moving into slightly restrictive territory on a risk-management basis, while underlying inflation remains contained. MUFG’s base case, given 45% probability, is continued French fiscal drift, with the deficit at 5.6% to 6.0% of GDP, the French-German spread near 170 basis points, and EUR/USD in a 1.08 to 1.14 range. In a deeper credibility crisis (15%), it sees the spread above 200 basis points and EUR/USD between 1.02 and 1.10, with the ECB’s TPI potentially in focus. MUFG forecasts EUR/USD at 1.12 by year-end, recovering gradually to 1.18 by the third quarter of 2027. The European Central Bank is set to keep rates on hold at next week’s policy meeting, but MUFG argues the tightening cycle is not over, even as rising bond yields and French fiscal stress do some of the work for policymakers. In its October European outlook, MUFG said the bond market sell-off and growing fiscal risks in France have taken an October rate hike off the table. ECB officials have increasingly pointed to the impact of tighter financial conditions on the outlook, and underlying inflation pressures remain contained. Even so, the bank’s strategists argue that resilient economic activity and higher gas prices since September still justify a move into slightly restrictive territory as a risk-management measure. MUFG expects a 25 basis point hike in December and another in the first quarter of 2027, taking the policy rate to 3.00%. It then sees the ECB cutting back to 2.75% by the third quarter of 2027, a path that assumes energy supply risks fade. France is at the centre of the outlook. MUFG notes that a fragmented parliament has led successive governments to miss fiscal targets repeatedly, leaving the deficit close to 6% of GDP despite several consolidation plans. With public debt around 120% of GDP, the bank says France has little room for further slippage and is highly exposed to weaker growth or a rise in borrowing costs. The IMF’s latest forecasts already show France as the clear outlier among major European economies, with growth seen at just 0.4% this year. The strain is visible in the bond market. The spread between French and German 10-year yields has widened to levels last seen during the euro zone debt crisis, while France’s annual interest bill has climbed to a record. MUFG suggests that a high and rising share of French debt held by foreign investors may have amplified the sell-off. Contagion has so far been limited, with Italian spreads relatively contained. The bank sets out four scenarios ahead of France’s presidential election, in which it describes Marine Le Pen as the frontrunner. Its base case, given 45% probability, is continued drift: the government survives by relying on procedural mechanisms, measures are diluted or delayed, and the deficit stays between 5.6% and 6.0% of GDP. In that case, MUFG sees the French-German spread around 170 basis points and EUR/USD in a 1.08 to 1.14 range. It would not force an immediate ECB response, but quantitative tightening could come under review. A deeper credibility crisis, at 15%, would bring acute political instability, a recession and a deficit well above 6% in 2027. That would push the spread above 200 basis points and drive EUR/USD down to between 1.02 and 1.10, with investors looking to the ECB’s Transmission Protection Instrument as a potential backstop. On the more positive side, limited consolidation (35%) would leave the spread near 110 basis points, while faster consolidation (5%) would narrow it to about 90 basis points and support EUR/USD in a 1.12 to 1.18 range. For the currency, MUFG says the scaling back of ECB hike expectations has already helped weaken the euro, which has closely tracked short-term rate differentials with the US. The bank expects the dollar to remain stronger for longer. It forecasts EUR/USD at 1.12 at the end of this year before a gradual recovery to 1.14 in the first quarter of 2027, 1.16 in the second and 1.18 in the third. With policymakers in their quiet period, next week’s statement and press conference will be watched for how much weight the ECB gives to tighter financial conditions and French fiscal risks, and whether it keeps the door open to a December move. This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.

articles.title: Far East Gold Ltd (ASX:FEG) Signs Strategic Alliance MoU to Pursue Gold Production and Portfolio Funding
articles.description: Far East Gold Limited (ASX:FEG) (OTCMKTS:FEGDF) announces that on 22 October 2026 it signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with PT Puncakbaru Jayatama (PTPJ) to pursue the potential acquisition, development and operation of the Bengkulu Gold Project and funding opportunities across FEG's existing portfolio. HIGHLIGHTS - Experienced operating partner: Established in 1991, PTPJ brings more than 30 years of Indonesian exploration and mining experience, including its longstanding involvement in exploration and mining operations at Gosowong, one of Indonesia's major high-grade gold operations with reported cumulative production exceeding six million ounces. - Potential pathway to gold production: Bengkulu's historical mining area, reported Production Operation licence status, existing pilot carbon-in-leach (CIL) plant and camp infrastructure provide a platform to assess a staged pathway to gold production. - Proposed controlling ownership: FEG intends to negotiate a staged acquisition of a controlling interest in Bengkulu, with ownership and consideration linked to agreed development and operational milestones. - Portfolio-wide funding strategy: The parties intend to combine FEG's existing asset portfolio, Bengkulu's potential production pathway and PTPJ's operating experience to attract strategic investment and project funding across FEG's portfolio. - Initial 90-day programme: An indicative timetable to progress independent valuations, commercial terms, development planning, financing proposals and definitive documentation. PTPJ has agreed to deal exclusively with FEG in relation to Bengkulu during this period. The MoU is principally non-binding. Acquisition terms and financing arrangements remain subject to due diligence, negotiation, definitive agreements and necessary approvals. Combining Indonesian operating experience with FEG's portfolio The proposed alliance combines FEG's existing exploration and development assets with PTPJ's technical and operating capabilities to assess a staged pathway to gold production at Bengkulu and pursue funding across the portfolio. FEG's portfolio forms a substantial part of its contribution. Its interests include two projects held under Contracts of Work and Trenggalek, which holds an IUP at the Production Operation stage. These assets, together with Idenburg's development potential and the broader portfolio's exploration upside, will be reflected in the independent valuations and commercial terms to be negotiated. PTPJ would coordinate engagement with the Bengkulu project and licence-holding entities and contribute technical expertise, operating relationships and access to prospective strategic and development partners. FEG would lead transaction structuring, capital markets activities and integration with its existing portfolio. Far East Gold Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer Shane Menere commented: "This strategic alliance is an important step in building Far East Gold into a broader gold exploration, development and potentially producing business. We have assembled a portfolio of highly prospective assets in Indonesia and Australia, and our priority now is to translate that potential into tangible value through disciplined development, access to capital and the right operating partnerships. I have known PTPJ President Director Daud Erikson Silitonga and members of his senior management team for many years, and we have developed a strong professional relationship built on mutual trust and respect. Pak Daud brings approximately 20 years of experience in exploration and brownfield project development, including a key role in discoveries at Gosowong. Our longstanding relationship reflects something I believe is fundamental to doing business successfully in Indonesia: trust, mutual respect and relationships built over time are invaluable assets that cannot simply be acquired, but must be earned. PTPJ brings decades of Indonesian exploration, development and operating experience, including involvement at Gosowong, one of Indonesia's world-class gold operations. Bengkulu's mining history and existing infrastructure provide a foundation to assess a staged pathway towards production, and together we intend to bring the technical expertise, operating teams and development planning needed to turn that opportunity into an executable project. In parallel, we will jointly pursue strategic investment and project funding options for Bengkulu and selected FEG assets. We have set a defined 90-day programme to advance the technical, commercial and financing arrangements, and our focus is on execution, responsible capital allocation and measurable progress for shareholders." PT Puncakbaru Jayatama President Director Daud Erikson Silitonga commented: "PTPJ brings more than three decades of Indonesian exploration and mining experience, including exploration, technical support and production with leading global operators. We see a strong opportunity to combine that practical experience with FEG's portfolio and listedcompany capabilities. Our intention is to help establish the technical team, operating plan and funding pathways required to advance Bengkulu towards production, while working together to attract strategic investment into FEG projects. We plan to build a lasting relationship that translates our combined experience and industry connections into operating capability, disciplined project development and long-term value." Bengkulu Gold Project - potential pathway to production The Bengkulu Gold Project is the principal development opportunity under the proposed alliance and has an established mining history. PTPJ has identified a northern open-pit prospect, a central historical mining area, reported Production Operation licence status, an existing pilot carbon-in-leach processing plant and associated camp infrastructure as a basis for assessing staged development. These features will be assessed through due diligence covering project ownership, mineral tenure, permitting, geology, metallurgy, processing infrastructure, environmental and community matters, operating readiness and development economics. The immediate objective is to establish the technical requirements, capital investment and approvals necessary to progress Bengkulu towards potential production. No production commencement date has been established. Proposed staged acquisition The MoU provides a framework for negotiating a Conditional Share Purchase Agreement under which FEG would seek to acquire a controlling interest in the company holding Bengkulu's project licences. The proposed transaction envisages three stages: 1. Initial acquisition: completion of due diligence, independent valuations and agreement of commercial terms, followed by an initial acquisition subject to necessary approvals. 2. Pilot commissioning: potential increased ownership linked to agreed commissioning, plant performance and operational milestones. 3. Commercial production and expansion: further ownership participation potentially linked to sustained production, verified resource growth or an approved expansion programme. The proposed structure is intended to align FEG's ownership and investment commitments with the achievement of agreed development milestones. Final ownership percentages, consideration, expenditure commitments and completion dates remain subject to negotiation. Any proposed FEG share consideration would be informed by independent valuations and an agreed pricing methodology, subject to applicable approvals. Initial 90-day implementation programme FEG and PTPJ have established an indicative programme to progress the collaboration towards definitive commercial arrangements. A joint working group is envisaged to coordinate technical assessment, independent valuation, transaction structuring, development planning and financing discussions. Milestones are measured from the date the MoU takes effect: Timing and Principal objectives Within 30 days: Exchange technical and commercial information, appoint independent valuers and seek agreement on a transaction term sheet. Within 60 days: Review initial due diligence findings and prepare preliminary development and funding plans. Within 90 days: Seek agreement on definitive transaction documentation and implementation arrangements. These milestones provide a framework against which progress can be assessed and reported to shareholders. The MoU has a six-month term and provides FEG with 90 days of project exclusivity, subject to its terms. All timeframes are indicative and remain subject to due diligence, negotiations and necessary approvals. Funding strategy across the FEG portfolio Securing development capital is a central objective of the proposed alliance. FEG and PTPJ intend to jointly prepare investment proposals for Bengkulu and existing FEG projects, supported by a coordinated programme of engagement with prospective strategic investors, financiers and development partners. Potential funding structures include strategic equity investment, project-level financing, joint ventures, earn-in agreements and offtake-linked arrangements. These alternatives will be assessed against project capital requirements, funding costs, ownership retention and potential shareholder dilution. As part of the initial 90-day programme, FEG intends to undertake a consolidated assessment of its anticipated capital requirements over the next 12-24 months, identifying priority development activities, associated funding needs and potential sources of capital. This assessment will form the basis of a coordinated financing strategy designed to advance selected projects while managing expenditure and protecting shareholder value. The strategy will also consider introducing development partners at individual project level, potentially reducing the requirement for FEG to fund all exploration and development expenditure directly. Over the longer term, should Bengkulu achieve profitable production, available operating cash flow could contribute to the development of FEG's broader portfolio, subject to project economics, financing obligations and ownership arrangements. Neither party has committed under the MoU to provide or procure funding. Next steps The immediate priorities are to progress Bengkulu due diligence, establish the commercial basis for the proposed acquisition and develop the associated project and portfolio funding plans. FEG will provide further market updates as material milestones are achieved, including progress on technical assessments, transaction negotiations, financing arrangements and definitive agreements. The Company's strategic objective remains to advance its existing portfolio while evaluating opportunities to strengthen operating capabilities, secure development capital and establish a potential pathway towards gold production. Status of the proposed transaction The MoU is non-binding except for provisions relating to confidentiality and market communications, term and termination, costs and exclusivity. It does not transfer project interests, issue FEG shares or establish binding acquisition, expenditure or financing obligations. Any transaction remains subject to satisfactory due diligence, independent valuations, agreement and execution of definitive documents by the relevant parties, and necessary board, shareholder, ASX and Indonesian regulatory approvals and third-party consents. There can be no assurance that definitive agreements will be executed, financing secured or production achieved. *To view tables and figures included in the announcement, please visit: https://abnnewswire.net/lnk/9G23UE5Y Justin Werner Chairman e:justin.werner@fareast.gold Shane Menere Chief Executive Officer e:shane.menere@fareast.gold m: + 61 406 189 672 + 62 811 860 8378 Tim Young Investor Relations and Capital Markets e:tim.young@fareast.gold m: + 61 484 247 771

articles.title: International study helps support FDA approval of HIV drug for newborns
articles.description: An international study conducted through the International Maternal Pediatric Adolescent AIDS Clinical Trials (IMPAACT) Network, including researchers at the University of California San Diego, helped inform the U.S. Food and Drug Administration's (FDA) recent approval of dolutegravir, a second-generation integrase inhibitor, for the treatment of human immunodeficiency virus (HIV-1) in newborns from birth. The study, published in The Lancet HIV, identified a dosing regimen that achieves appropriate drug levels in full-term newborns, supporting the use of dolutegravir to treat HIV from the first days of life.
